query:
The family treats the Sunday video call as a shared routine that everyone participates in. Based on what the conversations show, does this hold equally for all members — or does someone seem to relate to it differently, and what tells you that?

Options:
A. Emeka
B. Kayode
C. Tolu
D. Bisi
context:
[1] (about=Adaeze, episodic, t7 @2025-02-03T19:30:00) Good evening my children. Kayode, you have been on every call this month. I notice these things. God willing this continues.
[2] (about=Adaeze, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:27:00) The call happened. Your father was on for a little while. He said he needed to rest. God willing he is fine.
[3] (about=Adaeze, core, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Confirms Sunday call happened; Emeka was on briefly and said he needed to rest.
[4] (about=Nkem, core, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Thinks missing church is natural after a full day; asks if Sunday call happened.
[5] (about=Seun, episodic, t8 @2025-02-03T19:57:00) Nkem I love that you said that honestly I mean you are allowed to find it a lot, no one expects you to perform being fine with ten people in one room
agent_answer:
Emeka relates to the Sunday call differently.

Evidence: Adaeze notes that **Kayode** has been on “every call this month,” so Kayode fits the shared routine fully. But the call record shows **Emeka** was only on “for a little while” and “said he needed to rest” — so he did not participate in the same full way.

For the others: **Tolu** and **Bisi** have no record in the material showing how they relate to the call.

So the answer is **A. Emeka**.
